task_description: Guard the big-vs-small router: how often it sends a prompt to the branch a careful engineer would have chosen, measured on a held-out split the thresholds were never fitted on. Routing is a cost optimisation, so this guards against a regression that would quietly start sending hard prompts to the small model.
models: convaiinnovations/laya fine-tuned on the v1 ledger set, served through laya-mlx; questions are laya.router_questions() difficulty and is_sensitive

metric.unit: share (0-100) of the 24 held-out prompts routed to the branch the label names

tuned_on: the 48-prompt train split of the same file; the 24 test prompts are never fitted on

baselines.name: chance
baselines.notes: The eval set is balanced 36/36, so a coin flip scores 50.

baselines.name: shipped thresholds, 2026-09-22
baselines.notes: difficulty 1.6, is_sensitive 0.3, fitted on train by minimising expected cost. 17/24, 95% CI 54.17 to 87.5. n=24 so the interval is wide. FINDINGS §15.

baselines.name: fitted on accuracy instead of cost
baselines.notes: Four points higher and a worse router: 5 expensive mistakes instead of 3. Recorded so nobody 'improves' the score by switching the objective back.

contamination.notes: All 72 prompts were hand-written and hand-labelled by one engineer, so the labels are a judgment and not ground truth. Thresholds are fitted on the train split only. No real user traffic is in this file; replacing it with outcome-labelled real prompts is the stated next step.

prediction.statement: The router beats chance on prompts it was not fitted on, by a margin wide enough not to be resampling noise. Registered as a regression gate after the first measurement rather than blind, so it is set between chance (50) and the observed 70.83: a real regression fails it, ordinary noise does not.
